title: Scales & keys
examples: What is the difference between a major and a minor key?
How do I know what the key signature is?
Can you show me an example of a key signature?

explain.say: Today we are learning about musical scales and keys. A scale is a set of musical notes played in order. It gives the song its musical 'feel'.
The major scale sounds bright and happy to most people. It has a specific pattern of whole and half steps. This gives it its cheerful sound.
The minor scale sounds more sad or thoughtful. It uses a different pattern of steps than the major scale. This creates a different mood.
A key signature shows the notes that are sharp or flat for an entire piece. These sharps and flats apply throughout the music. It is like a musical rule.
If a piece has one sharp in the key signature, it is in the key of G Major. This tells you the notes to expect. It is a key guide.

draw.text: Key of G Major: One sharp

explain.say: In everyday life, think about a song you love. The key signature tells you what notes the song is built around. It keeps the song sounding consistent.

items: Music theory is like a set of rules.
The key signature is the main rule.
It keeps the song sounding right.

faq.q: What is the difference between a key and a key signature?
faq.a: The key is the central note or tonal center of a piece of music. The key signature is the collection of sharps or flats that are written at the beginning of the music to show the key.
asks: What does the key signature show?
Are the key and key signature the same thing?

faq.q: Does every song have a key signature?
faq.a: Most structured songs do have a key signature. It helps musicians know which notes to use correctly. Some very simple pieces might not show one.
asks: Do I always need to look for the key signature?
Can music exist without a key signature?

faq.q: Why does the major scale sound happy?
faq.a: The specific pattern of whole and half steps in the major scale is what gives it that characteristic bright sound. This pattern is mathematically consistent.
asks: What makes a major key sound happy?
Is the sound just an opinion?

faq.q: How do I remember the pattern for major and minor scales?
faq.a: You can remember the major scale pattern using whole and half steps. The minor scale has a slightly different pattern, which you need to learn.
asks: What is the step pattern for minor?
Can you give me a mnemonic for the scales?

faq.q: What does it mean if a piece is in the key of C?
faq.a: It means the piece is centered around the note C. The key signature will have no sharps or flats written for it. This is the simplest key.
asks: What is the easiest key to read?
If it's in the key of C, what notes can I use?

facts: The major scale has a specific pattern of whole and half steps.
The minor scale has a different step pattern than the major scale.
A key signature indicates sharps or flats for the entire piece.
The key of C has no sharps or flats in its key signature.

quiz.say: A piece of music with a bright, cheerful sound is most likely in which type of scale?
quiz.why: The major scale is constructed with a pattern that generally produces a bright and happy sound.

wrong.1: The minor scale is typically associated with a sadder or more thoughtful mood.
wrong.2: The chromatic scale uses every note, which sounds very different from a defined key.
wrong.3: The pentatonic scale omits certain notes, which changes the overall tonal quality.

quiz.say: If a key signature shows one sharp, which key is it most likely to be?
quiz.why: The key of G Major naturally requires one sharp, which is the F sharp, in its key signature.

wrong.1: F Major requires one flat, not a sharp, in its key signature.
wrong.2: D Major requires two sharps, so one sharp is incorrect.
wrong.3: C Major has no sharps or flats in its key signature.

quiz.say: If the key signature has no sharps or flats, what is the simplest key?
quiz.why: C Major is the foundational key because its natural notes require no alteration of sharps or flats.

wrong.0: G Major requires one sharp, which is not zero sharps or flats.
wrong.1: F Major requires one flat, which is different from having no sharps or flats.
wrong.3: A Minor is a relative minor and often requires a key signature to clarify its tonality.
